headline: Nvidia Slides 8.28% as Investors Flee the AI Trade, Pulling Chip Stocks and the Nasdaq Sharply Lower
body_html:
Nvidia fell 8.28% in early trading Wednesday, the day's dominant story, as investors pulled back from the artificial-intelligence trade. A surprise inflation reading added to the pressure, and Anthropic was caught up in the same selloff. Chipmakers were already sliding before the opening bell, and prices remain preliminary.

The damage spread quickly. The S&P 500 moved down 2.91% and the Nasdaq dropped 4.30%. Of the 654 stocks we track, only 84 rose while 567 fell. Semiconductors fell an average of 7.10%, the worst of any sector, and Technology lost 3.14%. Micron sank 10.18%, AMD fell 8.69%, TSMC dropped 7.02%, Broadcom lost 6.75% and Tesla slipped 5.85%.

Few places offered shelter. Consumer Staples gave up just 0.13% and Energy fell 1.08%. Ambarella was the standout loser, down 25.11%. The inflation data and the Federal Reserve's response to it remain the focus through the day. Thursday is a U.S. market holiday, and Friday is a half-day, with markets closing at 1:00 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Chip sector takes the brunt
briefs.body: Semiconductors averaged a 7.10% decline, far worse than any other group. Micron fell 10.18% and AMD lost 8.69%, with headlines describing investors fleeing the AI trade. Credo Technology and Astera Labs each gave up more than 10%.

briefs.headline: Broadcom tied to Anthropic's fortunes
briefs.body: Broadcom fell 6.75% as the market asked why it was sliding. Reports note the company took part in Anthropic's public offering and has a large further commitment riding on its success. Anthropic's own weakness is weighing on sentiment.

briefs.headline: Defensive pockets hold up
briefs.body: Drugmakers led the small group of gainers. Roche rose 3.50% and Sanofi gained 3.24%, while MINISO added 3.90%. Consumer Staples slipped only 0.13%, the mildest sector move, as investors looked for shelter outside technology.

briefs.headline: Heavy losses beyond the megacaps
briefs.body: Ambarella dropped 25.11% and Nutanix fell 20.68%. Celestica lost 12.93%, and Urban Outfitters, outside technology, declined 11.42%. The scale of these moves shows the selling reaching well past the biggest names.

briefs.headline: Gulf tensions keep Energy in view
briefs.body: Headlines reported Iran saying ships hit mines in Hormuz and the Houthis claiming an attack on a Saudi refinery. Even so, Energy fell an average 1.08%, a smaller drop than most sectors. Traders will watch whether the supply risks begin to lift the group.

briefs.headline: Holiday calendar shapes the day
briefs.body: Thursday is a U.S. market holiday, so today is the last full session of the week. Friday is a half-day with markets closing at 1:00 p.m. ET. Investors may be reluctant to carry large positions into the break, and Kevin Warsh's approach to reading market signals is being tested.
